'''Elizabeth Anne Kerekere'''<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20201125_039660000/event|title=Event – New Zealand Parliament|website=www.parliament.nz|access-date=10 December 2020}}</ref> (born {{Birth based on age as of date|47|2013|5|1|noage=1}})<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url= https://www.eit.ac.nz/2013/05/life-for-multi-media-artist-elizabeth-kerekere-is-very-much-a-planned-affair/|title=Life for multi-media artist Elizabeth Kerekere is very much a planned affair|website=[[Eastern Institute of Technology]] Hawke's Bay and Tairāwhiti|date=May 2013|language=en|access-date=20 February 2019}}</ref> is a New Zealand politician and LGBTQ activist and scholar.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=Dr Elizabeth Kerekere |language=en |website=[[Whakaata Māori|Māori Television]] |url=https://www.maoritelevision.com/election/candidates/dr-elizabeth-kerekere |access-date=20 February 2019}}</ref> She was elected a [[Member of Parliament (New Zealand)|member of parliament]] for the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand|Green Party]] in [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020]], but resigned from the Greens on 5 May 2023, following allegations of bullying within the party. Kerekere remained in parliament as an [[Independent politician|independent]] until the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 election]].<ref name="NZH Kerekere resignation">{{cite news |last=Coughlan |first=Thomas | url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/elizabeth-kerekere-breaks-silence/5PZ2JDCA5ZB4RK7ACICLU3EHKI/ | title=Green MP Elizabeth Kerekere resigns from party |date=5 May 2023 |access-date=10 May 2023|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]]}}</ref>

Kerekere identifies as ''{{Lang|Mi|[[takatāpui]]|italic=no}}'' and produced the first major research on {{Lang|Mi|takatāpui|italic=no}} identity with her doctoral thesis in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Takātapui |url=http://www.newzealandlgbtiawards.com/tak256tapui.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190122041315/http://www.newzealandlgbtiawards.com/tak256tapui.html |archive-date=22 January 2019 |access-date=20 February 2019 |website=New Zealand LGBTI Awards}}</ref><ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Kerekere |first=Elizabeth |date=2017 |title=Part of the Whānau: The Emergence of Takatāpui Identity – He Whāriki Takatāpui |url=http://researcharchive.vuw.ac.nz/handle/10063/6369 |type=PhD |publisher=Victoria University of Wellington}}</ref> She is also an artist and graduated from [[Eastern Institute of Technology]] with a bachelor in [[Māori people|Māori]] visual arts ({{Lang|Mi|Te Toi o Ngā Rangi}}).<ref name=":2" /> In 2000, in her role of Te Kairuruku, Ngā Kaupapa Māori at [[Dowse Art Museum]] she curated an exhibition called ''Kaumatua Anō te Ātaahua: Honouring the Gifts of our Elders''.<ref>{{Cite book|url=|title=Kaumātua : anō te ātaahua = Honouring the gifts of our elders|date=2001|publisher=Te Puni Kōkiri|others=Kerekere, Elizabeth., Twist, Nicholas., New Zealand. Te Puni Kōkiri., Lower Hutt (N.Z.). Dowse.|isbn=1-86953-513-8|location=[Wellington, N.Z.]|pages=|oclc=53315308}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Kerekere was born in [[Gisborne, New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.greens.org.nz/elizabeth_kerekere |title=Elizabeth Kerekere |publisher=Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand}}</ref> Her father, Karauria Tarao "Bison" Kerekere, was an artist and master carver.<ref>{{Cite web|date=26 November 2020|title=Artists Infiltrate Parliament|url=https://www.thebigidea.nz/stories/artists-infiltrate-parliament|access-date=12 January 2021|website=The Big Idea|language=en}}</ref> He was [[Māori people|Māori]], and of the [[Te Whānau a Kai]], [[Te Aitanga-a-Māhaki]], [[Rongowhakaata]], [[Ngāi Tāmanuhiri]] and [[Ngāti Oneone]] iwi.<ref name=":0" /> Elizabeth's mother Erin is Irish, from County Clare and County Tipperary.<ref name=":1">{{cite web |url=https://times-age.co.nz/candidates-housing-and-poverty-focus/ |title=Candidate's housing and poverty focus |date=3 July 2020 |work=Wairarapa Times-Age |first=Karen |last=Coltman }}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Kerekere is a lesbian,<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/kahu/elizabeth-kerekere-speaks-on-maori-lgbtq-term-takatapui/OYZLT7NZUNUERWBSABOZQ3LME4/ |title=Elizabeth Kerekere speaks on Maori LGBTQ term takatāpui |date=3 October 2017 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |first=Sarah |last=Harris}}</ref> and is married to Alofa Aiono, whom she met in 1992.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kerekere, Elizabeth; Mallard, Trevor|url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/pb/hansard-debates/rhr/document/HansS_20210210_052500000/kerekere-elizabeth-mallard-trevor |date=10 February 2021 |publisher=[[New Zealand Parliament]]}}</ref> The couple held their [[civil union]] in [[Te Papa]]'s marae, Te Marae Rongomaraeroa, which Kerekere advised on the design of in the late 1980s.<ref name=":1" />

== Activism ==
Kerekere was introduced to activism at a young age. She was 12 years old when she began babysitting the children of Māori women who held [[Consciousness raising|consciousness-raising]] meetings at their homes, and by age 15 was a junior member of the [[Māori Women's Welfare League]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite book |title=Takatapui: a Place of Standing |publisher=Oratia Media |year=2016 |editor-last=Harris |editor-first=Jordan |location=Auckland |pages=140–142}}</ref> As a teenager Kerekere was part of both the Māori and Black Women's movements, involved in a variety of political groups including [[Pacifica Inc|Young PACIFICA]] and the Ōtepoti Black Women's Group.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Elizabeth Kerekere - homosexual law reform » PrideNZ.com |url=https://www.pridenz.com/elizabeth_kerekere_homosexual_law_reform.html |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=www.pridenz.com}}</ref> In the 1980s, she also campaigned in the [[Anti-nuclear movement in New Zealand|nuclear free]] and [[Homosexual Law Reform Act 1986|homosexual law reform]] movements, and joined Māori and Pacific lesbian activist group Ngā Wāhine mō Ngā Wāhine o Te Moananui-a-Kiwa.<ref name=":3" /><ref name=":5" />

In 1998, Kerekere and Aiono attended the fifth [[Gay Games]] in [[Amsterdam]], which inspired Kerekere to lead a delegation to the sixth Gay Games in [[Sydney]] in 2002.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Kerekere |first=Elizabeth |date=2019 |title=Tīwhanawhana Trust |url=https://nzhistory.govt.nz/women-together/tiwhanawhana-trust |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=NZ History}}</ref> Between 1998 and 2002, Kerekere ran a weekly lotto fundraiser to make sure that Māori, Pacific, and low income lesbians would be represented on the team. Her desire for Māori representation in the Gay Games was also a motivation behind establishing the Tīwhanawhana Trust, which she did in 2001 with support from Māori women's performing trust Tī Kouka.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tiwhanawhana 20 Years On - interviews » PrideNZ.com |url=https://www.pridenz.com/tiwhanawhana_20_years_on_interviews.html |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=www.pridenz.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last=Kerekere |first=Elizabeth |date=2015 |title=Takatāpui |url=https://mentalhealth.org.nz/resources/resource/takatapui-part-of-the-whanau |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190221111939/https://www.mentalhealth.org.nz/assets/A-Z/Downloads/Takatapui-Part-of-the-Whanau.pdf |archive-date=21 February 2019 |access-date=17 December 2022 |publisher=Tīwhanawhana Trust and Mental Health Foundation |publication-place=Auckland |isbn=978-1-877318-91-7}}</ref>

Kerekere wrote that Tīwhanawhana has aimed "to uplift the mana of takatāpui both through Māori language and culture, and by advocating for takatāpui rights, health and well-being."<ref name=":4" /> Kevin Haunui began running Tīwhanawhana's weekly [[kapa haka]] group in [[Wellington]] from the mid-2000s, with Kerekere leading political work across various sectors relevant to takatāpui.<ref name=":4" /> In 2015, the Tīwhanawhana Trust board consisted of Kerekere, Haunui, Peri Te Wao, and Heta Timu.<ref name=":3" /> Since its foundation, Tīwhanawhana has become an integral part of Wellington's rainbow communities, often guiding the [[Tikanga Māori|tikanga]] – Māori cultural practices – at events and within organizations, informing organizational strategies so that they honor takatāpui, leading [[Waiata (Māori)|waiata]], and giving kapa haka performances.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tag: Tīwhanawhana » PrideNZ.com |url=https://www.pridenz.com/tags/1046.html |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=www.pridenz.com}}</ref> In 2019, Kerekere and Haunui led Tīwhanawhana as one of the host organisations – alongside [[Intersex Aotearoa]] and [[Rainbow Youth]] – in hosting the [[International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association|ILGA World]] conference.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ILGA World Conference 2018 |url=https://www.wellington2019.nz/host-ropu |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=www.wellington2019.nz}}</ref>

Long active in queer youth work, in 2007 Kerekere was involved in the [https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/CU0611/S00328/kaha-a-queer-youth-leadership-hui.htm KAHA Queer Youth Hui 2007], for which she created her first takatāpui youth group guidelines.<ref name=":3" /> In 2008 she took on a role with the OUT THERE! National Queer Youth Development Project, which provided education, resources and support for developing youth groups.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sexuality, gender identity and depression |url=http://www.bestpractice.net.nz/resources/depression/ld_sexuality.pdf |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=The Lowdown}}</ref> Through this role she organized the KAHA National Queer Youth Hui 2009, travelling nationally and developing relationships with youth groups.<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Tag: KAHA Youth Hui (2009) » PrideNZ.com |url=https://www.pridenz.com/tags/332.html |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=www.pridenz.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Kaha National Queer Youth Hui Participantion Up 200% |url=http://www.voxy.co.nz/national/kaha-national-queer-youth-hui-participantion-200/5/7717 |access-date=26 April 2023 |website=www.voxy.co.nz |language=en |archive-date=26 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230426033654/http://www.voxy.co.nz/national/kaha-national-queer-youth-hui-participantion-200/5/7717 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Throughout her studies at the [[Eastern Institute of Technology]] (EIT), Kerekere focussed on ''mana tūpuna'' (ancestors), ''mana wāhine'' (women) and ''mana [[takatāpui]]'' (the right to live and love regardless of sexual orientation and gender identity) and was the only degree graduate to have a solo exhibition.<ref name=":2" /> After graduating from EIT, Kerekere spent the following five years researching the development of takatāpui identity in the 21st century at [[Victoria University of Wellington]],<ref name=":2"/> arguing that pre-colonial Māori were sexually experimental people who openly accepted gender and [[sexual fluidity]],<ref>{{Cite news |url= https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=11879651 |title=Elizabeth Kerekere speaks on Maori LGBTQ term takatāpui |last=Harris |first=Sarah |newspaper=The New Zealand Herald |date=2 October 2017 |access-date=20 February 2019 |issn=1170-0777}}</ref> and completing a [[PhD]] in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://takatapui.nz/author#about-the-author |title=About the author |publisher=Rainbow Youth & Tīwhanawhana Trust |access-date=18 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite thesis |last=Kerekere |first=Elizabeth |year=2017 |type=Doctoral thesis |title=Part of The Whānau: The Emergence of Takatāpui Identity – He Whāriki Takatāpui |publisher=Open Access Repository Victoria University of Wellington, Victoria University of Wellington |doi=10.26686/wgtn.17060225 |url=https://openaccess.wgtn.ac.nz/articles/thesis/Part_of_The_Wh_nau_The_Emergence_of_Takat_pui_Identity_-_He_Wh_riki_Takat_pui/17060225/1|doi-access=free |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Kerekere stood in the [[Ikaroa-Rāwhiti]] electorate for the [[Green Party of Aotearoa New Zealand]] in the [[2017 New Zealand general election]]. She placed third of three candidates with 1,924 votes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Official Count Results – Ikaroa-Rawhiti|url=http://electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/electorate-details-66.html|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]|access-date=20 May 2019}}</ref> Her list placing of 19th was too low for her to enter parliament as a list MP.

Kerekere contested Ikaroa-Rāwhiti for the Green Party again in [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Ikaroa-Rāwhiti – Official Result |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/electorate-details-67.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=13 November 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Green Party list ranking revealed: can this group lift them over the threshold? |url= https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/25-05-2020/the-greens-list-ranking-revealed-can-this-group-lift-them-over-the-threshold/ |last=Manhire|first=Toby | author-link=Toby Manhire |date=25 May 2020 |work=[[The Spinoff]] |access-date=25 May 2020}}</ref> Although she again did not win Ikaroa-Rāwhiti, Kerekere entered parliament ninth on the Green Party's list.<ref>{{cite web |title=2020 General Election and Referendums – Official Result Successful Candidates |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/successful-candidates.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=13 November 2020}}</ref> Upon her election, and until her resignation from the Green Party in May 2023, she was appointed the Green Party deputy musterer ([[Whip (politics)|whip]]) and spokesperson for arts, culture and heritage, the community and voluntary sector, health, Māori development, rainbow communities, statistics, and [[Whānau Ora]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |date=18 July 2023 |title=Kerekere, Elizabeth – New Zealand Parliament |url=https://www.parliament.nz/en/mps-and-electorates/members-of-parliament/kerekere-elizabeth/ |access-date=8 July 2023 |website=www.parliament.nz |language=en}}</ref> She is a member of the health select committee and the [[Pae Ora (Healthy Futures) Act 2022|Pae Ora legislation]] committee.<ref name=":6" />

=== COVID-19 household isolation breach ===
On 15 March 2022, Kerekere resigned from her position as the Green Party spokesperson for health and acting spokesperson for COVID-19 response after she broke [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 isolation rules]] by flying from Gisborne to Wellington despite being a household contact for COVID-19. She was also temporarily removed from her position on the Health [[New Zealand House of Representatives committees|Select Committee]]. The Green Party also notified health authorities of the breach. Kerekere apologised for her actions and stated that she would cooperate with investigators.<ref>{{cite news |title=Green Party MP Elizabeth Kerekere breaks self-isolation rules |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/463342/green-party-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-breaks-self-isolation-rules |access-date=16 March 2022 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=15 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315090612/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/463342/green-party-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-breaks-self-isolation-rules |archive-date=15 March 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Small |first1=Zane |title=Green Party COVID-19 spokesperson Elizabeth Kerekere's isolation breach unearthed by 'disappointed' co-leader Marama Davidson |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2022/03/green-party-covid-19-spokesperson-elizabeth-kerekere-s-covid-19-isolation-breach-unearthed-by-disappointed-co-leader-marama-davidson.html |access-date=16 March 2022 |work=[[Newshub]] |date=15 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220315084629/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2022/03/green-party-covid-19-spokesperson-elizabeth-kerekere-s-covid-19-isolation-breach-unearthed-by-disappointed-co-leader-marama-davidson.html |archive-date=15 March 2022|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Bullying behaviour allegations ===
In early April 2023, the Green Party launched an investigation into Kerekere after she allegedly disparaged fellow Green MP [[Chlöe Swarbrick]] in a leaked group chat.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Green MP Elizabeth Kerekere calls Chlöe Swarbrick a 'crybaby' in group chat |language=en |work=[[Newshub]] |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/04/green-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-calls-chl-e-swarbrick-a-crybaby-in-group-chat.html |date=6 April 2023|access-date=7 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407075805/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/04/green-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-calls-chl-e-swarbrick-a-crybaby-in-group-chat.html|archive-date=7 April 2023|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Neilson |first1=Michael |title=Green MP Elizabeth Kereke investigated by party after 'crybaby' swipe at Chlöe Swarbrick |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/green-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-investigated-by-party-after-crybaby-swipe-at-chloe-swarbrick/CKFW2OPFCJBIVFR6X6E6KWSV7Q/ |access-date=8 April 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=7 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230407065444/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/green-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-investigated-by-party-after-crybaby-swipe-at-chloe-swarbrick/CKFW2OPFCJBIVFR6X6E6KWSV7Q/ |archive-date=7 April 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> [[Radio New Zealand]] subsequently reported that at least seven current and former Green Party staff had made allegations of bullying and combative behaviour against Kerekere. In response, a Green Party spokesperson stated that Kerekere was undergoing an "internal process" being conducted by musterer [[Jan Logie]] and chief of staff Robin Campbell.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |title=Green Party sources accuse MP Elizabeth Kerekere of 'bullying' |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/488141/green-party-sources-accuse-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-of-bullying |access-date=24 April 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=21 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230421081557/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/488141/green-party-sources-accuse-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-of-bullying |archive-date=21 April 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |title=More Green members criticise Kerekere, say bullying targeted Māori, Pasifika |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/488574/more-green-members-criticise-kerekere-say-bullying-targeted-maori-pasifika |access-date=24 April 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=24 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230424234638/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/488574/more-green-members-criticise-kerekere-say-bullying-targeted-maori-pasifika |archive-date=24 April 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

In response to the bullying allegations, members of the Green Party's Te Mātāwaka (the Māori and Pasifika rōpu) and the Rainbow Greens voiced support for Kerekere. An unidentified former senior Māori Green Party advisor claimed that Kerekere was the victim of bullying and alleged "dirty politics." According to [[Stuff (company)|Stuff]], Kerekere's high fourth-place ranking in the draft Green Party list had "ruffled feathers" with the parliamentary caucus.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McConnell |first1=Glenn |title=Maori, Rainbow Greens say Elizabeth Kerekere bullying claim is 'dirty politics' |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/131840291/mori-rainbow-greens-say-elizabeth-kerekere-bullying-claim-is-dirty-politics |access-date=2 May 2023 |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=24 April 2023 }}</ref> In late April, supporters of Kerekere failed to delay the Green Party's list rankings until the investigation into Kerekere's conduct had been concluded.<ref>{{cite news |last1=McCulloch |first1=Craig |title=Bid to delay Green Party list ranking fails |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/488817/bid-to-delay-green-party-list-ranking-fails |access-date=6 May 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=27 April 2023}}</ref> In early May 2023, the party's GreenLeft Network endorsed Kerekere as a preferred candidate in the party's ranking process, effectively calling on members to rank her highly on the party list.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Coughlan |first1=Thomas |title=Left wing Greens endorse Elizabeth Kerekere, despite investigation |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/left-wing-greens-endorse-elizabeth-kerekere-despite-investigation/5PY57UNHAJGRZMWV3OPS7NGAPI/ |access-date=2 May 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=1 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230502171404/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/left-wing-greens-endorse-elizabeth-kerekere-despite-investigation/5PY57UNHAJGRZMWV3OPS7NGAPI/|archive-date=2 May 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 5 May 2023 Kerekere left the Green Party to sit as an [[Independent politician|independent]] and announced she would not stand at the [[2023 New Zealand general election|2023 election]]. Kerekere announced her decision during a [[Zoom (software)|Zoom]] call with Green members that night. During the Zoom call, Kerekere expressed frustration with delays in the Green Party's investigation into her behaviour and accused co-leaders [[James Shaw (New Zealand politician)|James Shaw]] and [[Marama Davidson]] of making it difficult for her to continue working with the party.<ref name="NZH resignation">{{cite news |last=Coughlan |first=Thomas | url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/elizabeth-kerekere-breaks-silence/5PZ2JDCA5ZB4RK7ACICLU3EHKI/ | title=Green MP Elizabeth Kerekere resigns from party |date=5 May 2023 |access-date=6 May 2023|work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |publisher=[[NZME]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505110310/https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/elizabeth-kerekere-breaks-silence/5PZ2JDCA5ZB4RK7ACICLU3EHKI/|archive-date=5 May 2023|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Newshub resignation">{{cite news|url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/05/elizabeth-kerekere-resigns-from-green-party-to-sit-as-independent-mp.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230505103958/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/05/elizabeth-kerekere-resigns-from-green-party-to-sit-as-independent-mp.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 May 2023 |title=Elizabeth Kerekere resigns from Green Party, to sit as independent MP |date=6 May 2023 |access-date=6 May 2023 |work=[[Newshub]] }}</ref> In response, Shaw and Davidson disputed Kerekere's allegations and defended the investigation process, stating that Kerekere had resigned before the process could be concluded.<ref name="Newshub resignation" /><ref name="NZH untruths">{{cite news |last1=Coughlan |first1=Thomas |title='Some untruths were told' – Marama Davidson and James Shaw confront Elizabeth Kerekere allegations |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/politics/some-untruths-were-told-marama-davidson-and-james-shaw-confront-elizabeth-kerekere-allegations/GNSJDGMECNDHZJIO3GM6VPXAIY/ |access-date=6 May 2023 |work=[[The New Zealand Herald]] |date=6 May 2023}}</ref> They also confirmed that the party did not intend to use the [[waka-jumping]] provisions of the [[Electoral (Integrity) Amendment Act 2018]] to expel Kerekere from Parliament.<ref>[https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/489387/watch-green-party-co-leaders-respond-to-resignation-of-mp-elizabeth-kerekere "Watch: Green Party co-leaders respond to resignation of MP Elizabeth Kerekere"] [[Radio New Zealand]] 
6 May 2023, retrieved 29 March 2025</ref> On 10 May, Kerekere ruled out joining [[Te Pāti Māori]] (Māori Party).<ref>{{cite news |title=Elizabeth Kerekere rules out joining Te Pāti Māori |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/489621/elizabeth-kerekere-rules-out-joining-te-pati-maori |access-date=18 August 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=10 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230816092759/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/489621/elizabeth-kerekere-rules-out-joining-te-pati-maori |archive-date=16 August 2023|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 16 August 2023, Kerekere gave her valedictory speech in Parliament. She criticised Shaw and Davidson, accusing them of making "unfounded and increasingly elaborate allegations against her." Kerekere also alleged she was denied natural justice and was not subject to a formal complaints process, which she described as an "epic failure of leadership."<ref>{{cite news |title=Elizabeth Kerekere blames 'epic failure of leadership' for departure from politics |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/495943/elizabeth-kerekere-blames-epic-failure-of-leadership-for-departure-from-politics |access-date=18 August 2023 |work=[[Radio New Zealand]] |date=16 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230816105842/https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/political/495943/elizabeth-kerekere-blames-epic-failure-of-leadership-for-departure-from-politics |archive-date=16 August 2023|url-status=live}}</ref> In an interview that day, Kerekere explained that the "crybaby" reference was to herself, and that she thought she was sending the message to her wife.<ref>[https://www.stuff.co.nz/politics/350477073/former-green-mp-dr-elizabeth-kerekere-comes-out-swinging-in-tell-all-interview-reveals-which-former-colleague-hurt-her-most "Former Green MP Dr Elizabeth Kerekere comes out swinging in tell-all interview, reveals which former colleague hurt her most"] [[Stuff (website)|Stuff]], 16 August 2023, retrieved 28 March 2025</ref>

===After parliament===

Kerekere unsuccessfully ran for election as a [[Gisborne District Council|Gisborne District councillor]] for the Tairāwhiti [[Māori wards and constituencies|Māori ward]] in the [[2025 Gisborne District Council election|2025 local elections]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Campbell |first1=Zita |title=Former Green MP Elizabeth Kerekere runs for Māori Ward |url=https://www.1news.co.nz/2025/08/08/former-green-mp-elizabeth-kerekere-runs-for-maori-ward/ |date=8 August 2025 |access-date=12 August 2025 |work=[[1News]] |language=en}}</ref>
